question:
Describe the `time` complexity of:
A) searching a number in an unsorted list
B) searching a number in a sorted list using binary search
C) sorting a list using bubble sort

Provide a brief explanation for each case (for example, justify why the complexity is O(n)).
student_answer:
A) Search number on an unsorted list: 
O(n) - Linear: Needs to check ea. item once

B) Search num. in sorted list w/ binary search:
O(log n) - Log-linear: Opens to middle, then decides which half, then continuously divides in half

C) Bubble sort:
O(n²) — Quadratic: Compares adjacent pairs then swaps to correct order. Loop-in-loop, ea. item compared w/ every other item
